facts.fact: The signed US-Kenya Cooperation Framework states that the Government of Kenya has already deployed TaifaCare HMIS, a hospital management system with clinical management, laboratory, pharmacy and billing modules, in 1,500 public health facilities; it gives no denominator and does not say how many of the 1,500 are primary clinics.

The Framework describes TaifaCare HMIS as the Government of Kenya's flagship solution for health facilities, deployed and maintained by the government under the Digital Health Act, 2023, with US-supported systems such as Kenya EMR to be transitioned to the Digital Health Agency under a plan due before 1 April 2026.

The five-year Framework signed on 4 December 2025 names TaifaCare HMIS and sets its deployment at 2,000 public and faith-based facilities by 2026, 4,000 by 2027 and 8,000 by 2028, with its pharmacy module in 50% of public and faith-based facilities by end 2027 and 100% by end 2028, against a US$175,000,000 data systems line.

The US Government intends to provide US$175,000,000 over the Framework for data systems (US$30m in 2026, US$75m in 2027, US$50m in 2028, US$10m in each of 2029 and 2030), covering TaifaCare HMIS enhancement, maintenance and scale-up including Kenya's electronic medical records systems, alongside logistics, laboratory and surveillance systems.

Under the Framework the Government of Kenya intends to keep investing in the Digital Superhighway and to pay all ongoing software licensing, cloud, hardware maintenance and replacement costs for the systems in the data systems paragraph that the US does not specifically pay for; it states the intention without an amount or budget line.

Kenya and the United States signed a five-year health Cooperation Framework on 4 December 2025 that commits to scaling TaifaCare HMIS from 1,500 public facilities to 8,000 public and faith-based facilities by 2028 with US$175,000,000 of US data systems funding.

note: TaifaCare HMIS is classed emr because the Framework says it includes comprehensive clinical management and calls the record an Electronic Health Record. It also sets a usage target, not a present state: over 50% of clinical encounters loaded within one year of rollout in a facility and 90% within two. No aggregate reporting system is described, so no HMIS fact; 'Automated Indicator Reporting' is listed only as a planned TaifaCare improvement.
